facts.text: South Williamson, once called Stone, was settled in the late 18th century on land owned by Benjamin Williamson and never had its own post office.
South Williamson lies in the Tug Fork valley that was the heart of the Hatfield‑McCoy feud between West Virginia's Hatfields and Kentucky's McCoys from 1865 to 1890.
The Norfolk and Western Railway arrived in the 1890s, opening South Williamson to large‑scale coal extraction and transport.
South Williamson is protected by a floodwall, built by the US Army Corps of Engineers in response to a devastating flood along the Tug Fork River in 1977.
South Williamson's median age is 55.9, noticeably older than Kentucky's state median of 39.1.
The community borders the state of West Virginia along the Tug Fork River, lying directly across from the city of Williamson, West Virginia.
